# Interview Realtime Copilot

> Interview Realtime Copilot is an AI interview assistant for Mac and Windows: it transcribes and translates the interviewer live, detects each question and hints an answer from your own resume. Free plan.

Website: https://copilot.xichiuk.com/ · Download: https://copilot.xichiuk.com/download.html · Support: linkyourfuture2026@outlook.com · Updated 2026-11-19

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Interview Realtime Copilot?

Interview Realtime Copilot is an AI interview assistant for Mac. During a live interview it transcribes the interviewer, translates between English and Chinese, recognises each finished question and shows a short answer built from your own resume and notes. It also runs spoken mock interviews and writes a debrief after every session.

### How does it help if my English is not fluent?

Every sentence the interviewer says appears on screen with a Chinese translation as it is spoken, and each answer hint is written in natural English you can say directly, with a Chinese version beside it.

### Can it help with coding interview questions?

Yes. Press ⌥S and it reads the coding problem on your screen and returns a complete solution in your chosen language, with the approach to say out loud, time and space complexity, and edge cases. In our own evaluation its code passed the tests for ten of ten problems, from easy to hard.

### Can the interviewer see it?

The cockpit window is excluded from screen sharing and screen recordings by default, so it is not included when you share your screen in a meeting app.

### Where is my data stored?

Your resume, notes, transcripts, debriefs and recordings are stored on your own Mac. Audio and the text needed to answer are processed by our AI engine only during a session you start.

### How much does it cost?

There is a free plan with a monthly AI allowance, enough for about two practice sessions. Pro costs £25 a month or £169 a year and includes 20 times the free allowance. Local tax is added at checkout.

### Which computers does it run on?

Macs with Apple Silicon (M1 to M4) running macOS 14.2 or later, and 64-bit PCs on Windows 10 (2004+) or Windows 11.

## Use cases

- **Video interviews on Zoom, Teams or Meet**: The copilot hears the meeting and your microphone separately, recognises each question once the interviewer finishes, and streams a one-minute answer built from your resume — while you keep eye contact.
- **Interviewing in your second language**: Every interviewer line is translated as it is spoken (English ↔ Chinese), and hints come in both languages, so you understand precisely and answer fluently.
- **Technical and coding rounds**: Press ⌥S — or let auto-capture do it — and the copilot reads the coding problem, diagram or error on your screen and explains a solution with its trade-offs.
- **Rehearsing your prepared Q&A**: Upload your preparation document and every prepared question is extracted. A spoken AI interviewer asks them in order, at random or improvises, follows up once, and never repeats itself.
- **Getting stuck mid-answer**: Already talking? Expand answer continues from what you just said with the most valuable facts you have not mentioned yet, in under a minute.
- **Improving after every interview**: Each session ends with a debrief: every question reviewed, what was missing, a stronger spoken version — and the recording to replay.

## Pricing

Free plan with a monthly AI allowance; Pro is £25 a month or £169 a year with 20 times the allowance. Cancel anytime; local tax added at checkout.

# Getting started

## Help Center

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/

What Interview Realtime Copilot does, the loop it runs on, and how to find your way around this guide.

Interview Realtime Copilot is a Mac app that helps you through real job interviews. It listens to the interviewer, translates as they speak, recognises each question and shows a short answer built from your own resume and notes. It also rehearses with you before the interview and reviews every session afterwards.

New here? Install the app, sign in with your website account, create a goal and add your resume — then start a practice session. The realtime AI engine is ready as soon as you sign in; every plan includes a monthly allowance.

### The loop: Prepare, Practise, Perform, Review

Everything in the app follows the same four steps for each job you apply for. Go round the loop once per interview.

- **1. Prepare**: Create a goal (role and company) and add your resume and preparation notes.
- **2. Practise**: A spoken AI interviewer asks your prepared questions and follows up.
- **3. Perform**: Go Live in your real interview; the cockpit listens, translates and hints.
- **4. Review**: Read the debrief and replay the recording, then prepare better next time.

### Words you will see a lot

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Goal | One role at one company. Practice, live sessions and debriefs belong to a goal. |
| Knowledge sources | The resume and documents a session may use to answer. |
| Cockpit | The floating window you see during a session, hidden from screen sharing. |
| Hint | Three or four speakable bullets in English and Chinese. |
| Debrief | The review written after each session. |
| AI allowance | The monthly AI usage included in your plan. |

### Common questions

- Which Macs are supported? Apple Silicon (M1–M4) with macOS 14.2 or later.
- Does the interviewer see it? No — the cockpit is excluded from screen sharing and recordings.
- Need help? Email linkyourfuture2026@outlook.com.

## Install and sign in

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/install.html

Download the app, open it the first time, and sign in with your website account.

1. Download the installer for your system from the Download page — the DMG on macOS, the setup file on Windows.
2. On macOS, drag Interview Realtime Copilot into Applications. On Windows, run the setup file — it installs for your user, no administrator rights needed.
3. Open it. On macOS, preview builds are not yet notarised: System Settings → Privacy & Security → “Open Anyway”. On Windows, if SmartScreen appears, click “More info → Run anyway”.
4. Sign in with your email and password, or choose “Create an account”. It is the same account as on the website.

In mainland China, use the China site — copilot.xichigroup.com.cn — for much faster pages and downloads.

### Your workspace

Goals, documents, transcripts, debriefs and recordings are stored on your computer, in a workspace that belongs to your account. Signing out keeps them; signing in again opens them.

## Set up permissions

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/permissions.html

The microphone hears you; System Audio Recording hears the interviewer in your meeting app.

| Permission | Needed for | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Microphone | Practice and Live — your answers | Asked the first time you start a session |
| System Audio Recording | Live — the interviewer's voice | System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording |
| Screen Recording | Solve screen and auto-capture | Same panel as above |

Settings → Privacy & Stealth shows the state of each permission with a button to grant it. Preflight, the check before every session, lets you test the microphone level.

### On Windows

Windows asks for the microphone the first time a session starts. For Live, meeting audio is captured through the screen-and-audio sharing prompt the app shows — allow it with system audio enabled so the copilot can hear the meeting.

On macOS, after changing a permission in System Settings, quit and reopen the app so macOS applies it.

Prices exclude tax; your local VAT or sales tax is added at checkout.

- The allowance resets on the 1st of each month (UTC). Settings → Account shows what you have used and what is left.
- Spoken practice uses the most (realtime voice); live hints and translation use less; debriefs cost a few cents.
- When the allowance is used up, the cockpit says so; subscribe to Pro for a larger monthly allowance.

### Subscribe or manage billing

In Settings → Account click Subscribe (or Manage billing). The website opens already signed in; payment is handled by Stripe. Cancel anytime — Pro stays active until the end of the paid period.

## Your first interview, end to end

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/first-interview.html

From an empty app to a debrief in about fifteen minutes.

1. Create a goal: role, company and (ideally) the job description.
2. Add your resume and preparation notes on the goal's Prep tab. Wait until they show Ready.
3. Click Practice. In Preflight choose the practice mode and sources, test the microphone, and start.
4. Answer out loud. Use Suggest answer when you are stuck, or Expand answer to continue what you said.
5. Click End. The debrief appears in History within a minute.
6. On interview day, open your meeting app, click Go Live and keep the cockpit beside the call.

# Goals and materials

## Goals

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/goals.html

A goal is one role at one company; everything else hangs off it.

Create a goal from the sidebar. Add the job description so hints and practice questions focus on what the role needs. The goal page has three tabs: Overview, Prep (documents) and Sessions.

## Resume and preparation notes

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/materials.html

What to upload, what happens to it, and how prepared questions are found.

- Formats: PDF, Word (.docx), Markdown and plain text, up to 500 MB per file.
- Each document is read once and kept as text on your Mac, so large PDFs are only processed the first time.
- Every prepared question in your notes (Q&A, headings ending in “?”, numbered questions) becomes a practice question.

Hints only use facts from your materials. If something is not in them, the copilot suggests how to answer honestly rather than inventing experience.

### Knowledge sources

Preflight lets you choose which documents a session may use. The choice is remembered per goal.

# Practice interviews

## Spoken practice

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/practice.html

A spoken AI interviewer asks your prepared questions, waits for you to finish and follows up.

### Practice modes

| Mode | What happens |
|---|---|
| In order | Prepared questions in the order of your notes. |
| Random | Prepared questions shuffled; none repeated. |
| AI improvises | New questions based on the role and your answers. |

- The question panel shows progress (asked / total). Click any question to jump to it.
- The interviewer waits about 2.5 seconds of silence before replying, so pauses while you think are fine.
- Each question gets at most one follow-up, then the interview moves on.

### Help while answering

- Suggest answer — under an interviewer line: a bilingual hint for that question.
- Expand answer — under your own line: continues what you said with the facts you have not mentioned yet.

# Live interview

## Go Live

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/go-live.html

Start a live session for a real interview on Zoom, Teams, Meet or any call app.

1. Join the call in your meeting app.
2. Click Go Live on the goal. In Preflight choose the knowledge sources, answer language and playbook.
3. Start. The cockpit opens and both meters (Mic and Computer) should move when people speak.

### What you see

- Interviewer lines appear as they speak, with the translation underneath.
- Pauses inside a question do not split it; a finished question becomes a question card.
- A hint streams in: three or four bullets in English and Chinese, from your materials.
- If a question is cut off mid-sentence, a hint still appears after a short pause.

The copilot hears everything your Mac plays. Close music and videos during the interview so they are not transcribed.

## The cockpit and stealth

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/cockpit.html

Keep the cockpit readable for you and invisible to everyone else.

- Hide from screen sharing is on by default: the cockpit does not appear in shared screens or recordings. Turning it off shows a warning.
- Appearance: opacity 70–100% (default 80%), background and text colours, with a live preview.
- Move and resize it with the keyboard so you never reach for the mouse during a call.

## Keyboard shortcuts

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/shortcuts.html

Default shortcuts; change any of them in Settings → Shortcuts.

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Show or hide the results panel | ⌥ C |
| Solve screen | ⌥ S |
| Show or hide the cockpit | ⌥ A |
| Move the cockpit | ⌥ ↑ ↓ ← → |
| Wider / narrower | ⌥ =  /  ⌥ − |

## Coding, system design and screen help

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/solve-screen.html

Let the copilot read the problem on your screen and explain a solution.

- Press ⌥S (or Solve screen in the cockpit) to capture the screen once. The copilot reads the coding problem, diagram or error and writes a solution with its complexity and edge cases.
- Auto-capture (Settings → Privacy & Stealth) does this by itself when the interviewer asks a coding or system-design question.
- Defaults → Coding language sets the language solutions are written in.

Screen capture needs the Screen Recording permission. Only one screenshot is taken per request; nothing is recorded continuously.

# History and debriefs

## Debriefs and recordings

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/debriefs.html

Every session is recorded on your Mac and reviewed question by question.

- History lists your sessions; open one to read its debrief and play the recording.
- The debrief reviews every question (up to 40 per session): what was missing and a stronger spoken version, using only what you actually said.
- The recording mixes your microphone, the computer audio and the practice interviewer's voice. It is saved when you click End.

No debrief? A session needs some of your own speech to review. If the microphone was muted or denied, there is nothing to assess.

What stays on your Mac and what is sent for processing.

# Interview guides

## How to get through an English interview when English is not your first language

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/english-interview.html

A practical method for understanding every question and answering clearly — with and without an AI interview assistant.

### Why English interviews go wrong

- You miss part of the question — an accent, a fast speaker or an unfamiliar term — and answer something else.
- You know the answer in your own language but lose time translating it in your head.
- Nerves make both problems worse.

### Five things that work

1. Write your ten most likely answers in English beforehand, in short spoken sentences, and say them out loud.
2. Learn the English names of your own work: systems, metrics, tools. These are the words you cannot paraphrase.
3. Answer in a fixed shape: the direct answer first, then how it works, then one number or result.
4. If you did not catch a question, say “Let me make sure I understood — you are asking about …?” It is normal and buys time.
5. Rehearse with a spoken mock interviewer, not silently. Speaking is a different skill from reading.

### How an AI interview assistant helps

Interview Realtime Copilot shows every interviewer sentence with a Chinese translation as it is spoken, turns a finished question into a card, and gives you a short answer in natural English built from your own resume. Before the interview, its spoken practice asks your prepared questions out loud so the real one feels familiar.

Use the hints as a prompt for your own words. Reading a script aloud sounds unnatural; glancing at three bullets does not.

## Interviewing for an overseas remote job from your home country

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/overseas-remote-interview.html

Timezone math, English small talk and an unfamiliar meeting link — what is different about remote interviews for overseas companies, and how to prepare.

The work is the same; the interview is not. You are interviewed in a second language, at an odd hour, over a meeting link you may not have used — and remote teams judge communication almost as much as skill, because communication is the job when nobody shares an office.

### Before the interview

1. Confirm the time in writing with the timezone spelled out — “Wednesday 9 AM Pacific” — never “your morning”. Overseas teams book in their timezone; write it down in yours.
2. Test the meeting link a day early and install the desktop client rather than using the browser. From mainland China, check the link loads on your normal network; our China site (copilot.xichigroup.com.cn) downloads the app without a proxy.
3. Write a 60-second self-introduction in English and say it out loud ten times. The first two minutes set the tone for the whole call.
4. Learn the English names of your own work: systems, tools, metrics. These are the words you cannot paraphrase mid-sentence.
5. Prepare two questions to ask them — how the team works across timezones, what the first month looks like. Remote teams evaluate whether you communicate like someone easy to work with.

### During the interview

- Small talk is part of the test, not noise. Have two easy topics ready — your weekend, your workspace — and answer them warmly and briefly.
- Connection problems are normal. Keep the line ready: “Sorry, I think the connection dropped for a second — could you say that again?”
- Slow is fine. Pause for two seconds before answering rather than filling silence — on a laggy call, pauses read as thoughtfulness.
- Ask for the question in text if you need it — “Could you paste that in the chat?” — especially for multi-part questions.

### Where the copilot helps

Interview Realtime Copilot shows every interviewer sentence with a Chinese translation as it is spoken and hints short answers in natural English built from your own resume — so a missed phrase never turns into a wrong answer, and what you say still comes from your real experience. Sign in and downloads work directly from mainland China through the China site.

Hints are a prompt, not a script. Overseas interviewers probe with follow-ups; the experience must be yours or the next question exposes it.

## What is an AI interview assistant, and how do you choose one?

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/ai-interview-assistant.html

What these tools do during a live interview, what to check before trusting one, and where they do not help.

An AI interview assistant — some people call it an interview copilot, 面试神器 or 面试外挂 — is an app that listens to your interview, recognises the question and suggests an answer while you are still on the call.

### What to check

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Does it answer from your own resume and notes? | Generic answers are easy to spot; invented experience fails follow-up questions. |
| How fast is the first hint? | More than a few seconds and the silence is noticeable. |
| Does it understand questions with pauses? | Real interviewers think aloud; a tool that splits one question into three gives three wrong answers. |
| Is it hidden from screen sharing? | Otherwise the interviewer sees the window. |
| Can you rehearse with it? | The first time you use it should not be the real interview. |
| Where is your data kept? | Your resume and recordings are personal; local storage is safer. |

### Where it does not help

- It cannot give you experience you do not have — and a good tool will not pretend to.
- Check the rules of each interview and use it within them.

Interview Realtime Copilot is built around these points: answers from your own materials, question detection that survives pauses, English–Chinese translation, spoken practice, and local storage.

## Behavioral interview questions: how to answer with STAR and sound prepared

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/behavioral-questions.html

The questions are predictable — “tell me about a time…”. What makes answers land is the structure behind them.

Behavioral rounds measure how you worked, not what you know. Interviewers score each answer against a rubric — ownership, conflict, impact — so a rambling true story scores worse than a structured ordinary one.

### The STAR shape, in one minute

1. Situation — one sentence. Where, when, what team. Resist the urge to give background.
2. Task — one sentence. What was yours to fix, not the team's.
3. Action — most of your time. Three verbs: what you decided, what you did, what you changed when it went wrong.
4. Result — one number or one change that lasted. “Deploys went from weekly to daily” beats “it went well”.

### The eight questions that cover most rounds

| Question | What it probes |
|---|---|
| Tell me about yourself | Not a story — a 60-second arc: now, before, why here. |
| A conflict with a teammate | Whether you escalate or resolve; never “the other person was wrong”. |
| A time you failed | A real failure, what you changed afterwards. Humble-bragging fails here. |
| Your most challenging project | How you break down something too big; one deep story beats five shallow ones. |
| Disagreeing with your manager | Disagree with data, commit once decided. |
| Learning something fast | Your method, not your talent: how you found the 20% that mattered. |
| Why this company | Read their materials; name something specific, not “your great culture”. |
| Going beyond your job | Ownership without being asked — the rubric line every company shares. |

### Practice that transfers

Written STAR answers and spoken ones are different skills — the spoken version is half the length and needs signposts (“…and the result was”). Say each story out loud until it fits in ninety seconds. Interview Realtime Copilot turns your preparation notes into a spoken mock interview and reviews each answer in the debrief, so the structure is practised, not just drafted.

## Interview tomorrow and no time to prepare: a two-hour plan

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/last-minute-prep.html

What to do, in order, when the interview is close and preparation time is short.

1. 20 minutes — read the job description and underline the five skills it repeats. Those are your questions.
2. 30 minutes — for each skill, write one real example from your work: the situation, what you did, the result with a number.
3. 20 minutes — prepare the three certain questions: tell me about yourself, why this company, why are you leaving.
4. 40 minutes — say the answers out loud against a mock interviewer and fix the ones that ramble.
5. 10 minutes — check your microphone, camera and meeting link; sleep.

### Doing it faster with the copilot

Upload your resume, the job description and whatever notes you have. Interview Realtime Copilot extracts the questions, a spoken AI interviewer asks them, and during the real interview each hint is drawn from those same files — so the two hours you do have go into rehearsing rather than writing.

# Troubleshooting and FAQ

## Troubleshooting

https://copilot.xichiuk.com/docs/troubleshooting.html

Fixes for the problems people meet most often.

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| The Computer meter does not move in Live (macOS) | Allow System Audio Recording for the app, quit and reopen it, and check the meeting's sound plays through this Mac. |
| The Computer meter does not move in Live (Windows) | Restart Live and allow the screen-and-audio sharing prompt with “share system audio” enabled. |
| The Mic meter does not move | Allow the microphone in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone; check the input device in macOS Sound settings. |
| “Your monthly AI allowance is used up” | Subscribe in Settings → Account, or wait for next month's allowance. |
| macOS says the app cannot be opened | System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (preview builds are not notarised yet). |
| Windows says “Windows protected your PC” | Click More info → Run anyway (preview builds are not code-signed yet). |
| Cannot reach the account service | Check your internet connection or proxy; the app keeps you signed in and retries. |
| A continuous question is split into pieces | Usually a very long pause; the copilot still answers the combined question. Tell us if it keeps happening. |

### Contact support

Email linkyourfuture2026@outlook.com with what you did, what you expected and what happened. In the app, the Help button (?) opens a new email for you.
